name: Artemis II
first: First crewed flight beyond low-Earth orbit since Apollo 17 (1972) — and the mission that inspired this project
description: The Artemis program's first crewed flight, and the spark that became Orrery. On 1 April 2026 NASA's SLS Block 1 launched an Orion spacecraft with four astronauts — Reid Wiseman (CDR), Victor Glover (PLT), Christina Koch (MS), and CSA's Jeremy Hansen (MS) — onto a free-return trajectory that swung them around the Moon's far side about 6,500 km above the surface and brought them home without any lunar-orbit insertion burn. At 406,771 km from Earth they travelled farther than any humans before them, beating Apollo 13's 1970 record. After a 9-day flight Orion splashed down in the Pacific off San Diego on 10 April. The flight qualified Orion's life support, navigation and heat shield for crewed missions ahead of the first landing, now planned for Artemis IV.

events.label: SLS LAUNCH
events.note: Orion lifts off from KSC LC-39B with four crew aboard.

events.label: TLI
events.note: Trans-lunar injection burn by ICPS — Orion separates onto cislunar trajectory.

events.label: LUNAR FLYBY
events.note: Closest approach over the far side, ~6,500 km altitude, and the farthest humans have travelled: 406,771 km from Earth. No orbit insertion — free-return geometry slings Orion back to Earth.

events.label: SPLASHDOWN
events.note: Orion re-entry and Pacific Ocean splashdown.
